A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same risk-based uncertainty framework. All 12 pages of v1 and 24 pages of v2, including appendices, equations, figures and tables, support comparison. Relocated derivations and illustrations can be matched.

before.justification: V1 contains theoretical derivations and conceptual illustrations, including Appendix A, but no original experimental or data-analysis results.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendices E–J report original deep-ensemble experiments for out-of-distribution and misclassification detection, including numerical results in Tables 2–9.

M1.justification: V2 extends the Bayesian averaging choices to the predictive argument as well as the unknown distribution, adding posterior-mean predictor options and the zero-excess case (Section 4, Appendix C). The core risk framework, EPBD, reverse-Bregman estimate and risk-difference/BALD quantity already appear in v1.

E1.justification: V1 has no dataset-based evaluation. V2 introduces out-of-distribution and misclassification detection using CIFAR10, CIFAR100, SVHN, blurred and label-corrupted CIFAR variants, and a CIFAR10 scenario with classes omitted from selected ensemble members (Section 6, Appendix E).

E2.justification: V2 introduces empirical comparisons among Bayes-, total- and excess-risk measures. Tables 6–9 explicitly compare BI, RBI and EPBD, whose log-score instances are BALD, RMI and EPKL. V1 discusses these quantities mathematically but evaluates no comparators; the new comparisons are among uncertainty measures within the framework.

E3.justification: V2 adds an AUROC-based evaluation protocol using 20-member ResNet18 and VGG19 ensembles, log/Brier/spherical training losses, and matching versus mismatched uncertainty scoring rules. Main results aggregate approximation choices, while Appendix J separates them and excludes the identically zero excess-risk approximation. V1 contains no empirical protocol.

E4.justification: New analyses examine training/uncertainty-score matching, distribution shifts, label noise, class omissions and inner versus outer approximation strategies. Appendix G additionally excludes Neglog to test whether its instability alone explains the mismatch effect (Figure 7). V1 has no corresponding empirical ablations or robustness analyses.

E5.justification: V2 adds ensemble-member performance distributions (Figures 4–5), AUROC distributions and aggregate mean ± summaries in Appendix J. Those summaries describe variation across datasets or dataset pairs, rather than repeated full-ensemble trials. Seed identifiers, confidence intervals and significance tests are not reported.

E6.justification: V2 adds all empirical results in Tables 2–9 and the experimental plots. For CIFAR10 versus blurred CIFAR10, Table 2 reports excess/Bayes AUROC of 87.80/84.38; for noisy CIFAR100 misclassification, Table 3 reports Bayes/excess AUROC of 82.64/72.30. These are newly reported results, with no corresponding v1 measurements.

T1.justification: The core decomposition and score-specific risk derivations are retained, often relocated. V2 corrects the Bregman-divergence sign in v1 Equation (6), adds explicit loss derivations and relations involving the expanded approximation cases, and shifts spherical Bayes/total risks by a constant (Appendices A–D).

C1.justification: V2 adds empirical effectiveness and scenario-specific guidance as central contributions in the abstract, introduction and conclusion. V1 foregrounds the claim that BALD captures only part of epistemic uncertainty; v2 foregrounds a unified family containing BALD and EPKL, while retaining the partial-uncertainty argument in Appendix C.

C2.justification: V2 connects weak excess-risk performance on hard-OOD inputs to possible failure of the conditional-distribution approximation. It adds recommendations about matching training and uncertainty scores, choosing risks for noisy misclassification, and avoiding universal approximation rankings. These interpretations substantially extend v1's retained theoretical limitations (Section 6, Appendices G–J).

D1.justification: Unlike v1, v2 documents experimental implementation: label-swap pairs, ensemble-specific class omissions, Gaussian-blur parameters, architectures, 200 training epochs, SGD with momentum and weight decay, and learning-rate schedules. Appendix F also adds links to two training-code repositories, although some hyperparameter values are deferred to that code.

R1.justification: V2 adds targeted positioning relative to DEUP, Bregman information and bias–variance decomposition work, plus citations covering Bayesian approximations and the new experiments. The existing Bayesian, deterministic and second-order uncertainty taxonomy remains. Publication-metadata updates to retained references do not constitute new related work.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, Bayesian section and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Risk definitions and proper scoring rules become separate main sections, while much of the existing derivation and approximation discussion moves into Appendices A–D. This materially reorganizes the retained argument as well as accommodating the experiments.

P2.justification: V2 adds AUROC boxplots and histograms, ensemble-performance violin plots, and numerical comparison Tables 2–9. Table 1 receives revised labels and formatting. V1's risk-estimation diagram is retained as Appendix Figure 3, while the original illustrative Figure 1 remains.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the practical support for the framework. Section 6 and Appendices G–J test previously untested recommendations, reveal different behavior on soft versus hard OOD inputs, and check whether Neglog alone explains scoring-rule mismatch failures. The expanded approximation recipe, corrected mathematics and implementation details improve usability. Statistical reporting and some implementation details remain incomplete, but the direct evidence and clearer applicability boundaries provide substantial overall gains.
